findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow uses status: String combined with is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool, allowing invalid state combinations such as is_sent=false with status="sent", or status="sent" with is_validated=false
findings.failure_mode: Any status string and boolean flag combination is constructible at compile time, so corrupted or inconsistent workflow states can exist and propagate silently through the domain
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool with a single QuoteStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) that encodes the lifecycle invariants at the type level. Remove boolean fields entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a QuoteWorkflow with no typestate guard, so any caller can call mark_sent on a workflow in any state (including already-sent, never-validated, or arbitrary invalid states)
findings.failure_mode: Business logic invariant (a quote must be validated before sending) is not enforced by the type system, allowing double-sending or sending unvalidated quotes
findings.fix: Use a typestate pattern: define types like QuotePending, QuoteValidated, and QuoteSent. mark_sent should accept QuoteValidated and return QuoteSent. The compiler prevents calling mark_sent on QuotePending.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain meaning. Any string, including empty, malformed, or unrelated strings, is accepted as a quote ID.
findings.failure_mode: No domain-level invariants on IDs (non-empty, format, uniqueness) can be enforced at the type level, leading to potential collisions, empty IDs, or mixing unrelated string identifiers
findings.fix: Introduce a QuoteId newtype (e.g., pub struct QuoteId(String)) with a fallible constructor that enforces domain rules at the parse boundary. The core never sees raw strings.

findings.problem: All fields of QuoteWorkflow are pub, exposing the internal representation and allowing external mutation of internal state invariants
findings.failure_mode: External code can mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent directly, bypassing all domain logic and creating inconsistent states without any code change on the caller side
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a fallible smart constructor (e.g., QuoteWorkflow::new) and immutable getters. All mutations go through domain methods.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() which allocates a new String, and mutates the struct in place. The function has no purity guarantee and does not follow functional core discipline.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every call, and mutation of the input struct instead of producing an immutable derived value
findings.fix: In a typestate model, mark_sent would take owned QuoteValidated and return QuoteSent with no intermediate allocation. Status would be an enum variant (zero-cost), not a .to_string() call.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is redundant when is_sent: bool already exists. If is_sent is true, sent_at_epoch_ms should always be Some; if is_sent is false, it should always be None.
findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent state: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None loses the sent timestamp, or is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some records a sent time without marking the workflow as sent
findings.fix: Encode the sent timestamp directly in the Sent variant of the QuoteStatus enum (e.g., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }). The boolean and Option are eliminated entirely.

findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow has no constructor and is fully public. There is no parse boundary where raw primitives are validated into trusted domain types.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid QuoteWorkflow instances can be constructed from any data source without validation, violating the 'parse at boundaries into trusted data' rule
findings.fix: Add pub fn QuoteWorkflow::try_from_parts(id: &str, ...) -> Result<QuoteWorkflow, QuoteError> as the single entry point for creating instances, enforcing all invariants before construction.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler data for allocation patterns
no allocation audit (Vec/String allocation in mark_sent)
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy not run)
no behavior tests for the workflow lifecycle
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code has fundamental architectural violations: illegal states are fully representable, no typestate enforcement, no parse boundary, and all fields are publicly mutable. These are compile-time correctable issues but represent the most critical failure mode class in Holzman Rust.
